one_line_description.value: Ecwid is an ecommerce platform for customizing online stores, building headless storefronts, and creating merchant apps.
one_line_description.quote: Customize a store’s functionality or design, create headless sites, or build powerful apps that empower merchants selling around the world.

has_public_api.quote: Ecwid REST API allows you to access and manage any store data, payment and shipping methods, and storefront settings.

api_breadth.value: Broad REST API covering store profile, catalog, orders, customers, categories, discounts, payment and shipping methods, and storefront settings, with read and write operations.
api_breadth.quote: Ecwid REST API allows you to access and manage any store data, payment and shipping methods, and storefront settings.

auth_methods.quote: We use OAuth 2.0 authorization simplified for single-store customizations, JSON-formatted data, and a clear structure.

oauth_scopes_documented.quote: Access to Ecwid API features is limited by permissions called access scopes.

access_model.quote: Only stores on paid plans can access API.

access_notes.value: Only stores on paid plans can access API (free test-store plan upgrades are available by emailing Ecwid).
access_notes.quote: Only stores on paid plans can access API.

rate_limits.value: 600 requests per minute per token; exceeding the limit returns HTTP 429 with a Retry-After header; repeated requests from a non-working token can be blocked.
rate_limits.quote: We accept up to 600 requests per minute per token. If you exceed the limit, all subsequent requests will be ignored with an error 429 and a "Retry-After": N header (number N is a cooldown) . If more requests continue to come from a non-working token, Ecwid will block it for much longer

webhooks.quote: Webhooks are triggered by any changes in the store data, no matter their source.

sandbox_or_test_env.quote: We provide a developer with a paid subscription account in a test store for development and testing purposes.

verdict_reason: Ecwid exposes a broad REST API with OAuth 2.0, extensive scope-based read/write access, and webhooks. However, official setup docs state that only stores on paid plans can access the API. Public App Market distribution also involves a partner contract and app review, so the access path is not fully self-serve for all use cases.
main_blocker: Paid-plan Ecwid store required for API access
open_questions: No vendor-operated MCP server is documented in the fetched sources; search results only surfaced third-party MCP listings (Pipedream, Zapier, UsefulAPI) that were not among the fetched SOURCES.
Official SDK languages were not evidenced; only a 'community libraries' page appeared in search results and was not fetched.
API versioning/deprecation policy was not present in the fetched sources; changelog pages were returned by search but not included in the evidence bundle.
The exact eligibility and approval process for Ecwid's free test-store plan upgrade (email request) should be confirmed.
Community MCP server URLs could not be verified from fetched sources, so they are not listed.
